[2026-03-24 12:41] User asked to research seqlog.com and explain SeqLog in plain Chinese, including what it is for, who uses it, and use cases for personal and small-group users. Assistant established from the public site that SeqLog is a real macOS-native Logseq-style knowledge app focused on local-first Markdown files, wikilinks/backlinks, daily notes, and Apple-native SwiftUI + Rust/ripgrep performance positioning. During the conversation, two externally provided summaries were identified as incorrect: one falsely described SeqLog as an AI/agent logging 'black box' tool, and another treated SeqLog as an uncertain or generic timeline-log product rather than the actual macOS-native Logseq alternative. Useful future follow-up: provide a brief, plain-language DJClaw Chinese post and a 'SeqLog vs Logseq' comparison grounded in the real product.

[2026-03-25 14:17] User had a beginner Logseq discussion and then requested publication work. Assistant explained Page vs Backlink, Flashcard, and advised minimal plugins first. User chose title 1 and approved direct publish; DJClaw post 067 `posts-2026-03-25-067-logseq-basics-macbook-android.html` titled `Logseq 入门：Journal、Block、Page 到底是什么` was written, added to `index.html` and `sitemap.xml`, and pushed to `main` in commit `1414384` (`Publish post 067 on Logseq basics`). User then asked how Logseq data sync works between Android and MacBook; preserve the explanation that Logseq syncs the graph/data folder (journals/pages/logseq/assets) rather than an abstract account database, with two main approaches: official Logseq Sync or third-party file sync, and with Mac as main editor + Android as lightweight companion recommended. Later the user asked to read a WeChat article and a Digital Garden page, summarize them, write a DJClaw article in a Craig Adams-like style, and publish it. Retrieval failed: the WeChat page yielded only generic shell text via readability and the `tothegarden.vercel.app/page/数字花园` URL returned 404, so article writing/publishing could not proceed yet.

[2026-03-25 19:16] User pivoted the wiki project toward a Logseq-inspired architecture. Assistant concluded Logseq is suitable as a concept/kernel for the personal wiki (page/block/journal/backlink/graph-ready ideas) but should not be adopted wholesale as the product engine; the missing core is an extraction pipeline from HISTORY/chat/posts/commits into structured entities, events, relations, evidence, and timeline. User then requested: publish a clear technical architecture / layered design document to DJClaw, execute schema/design option B as the MVP basis, update the wiki GitHub repo issues/project to reflect MVP1/MVP2/MVP3 plus existing progress, and update the wiki README. During follow-up, assistant inspected /home/dj/.nanobot/workspace/wiki, confirmed repo djclaw/wiki with existing MVP4-labeled issues and GitHub Project 2 'Wiki', reviewed README/scripts/docs, and wrote a new README.md in the wiki repo. Also preserve that earlier on 2026-03-25 14:17, because Brave search was unavailable and source retrieval was partial (WeChat blocked by verification, Digital Garden SPA only partially parsable), DJClaw post 068 'A Small Digital Garden' was nevertheless published from accessible material in commit 778c069 with explicit caveat that no WeChat details were fabricated.

[2026-03-25 21:35] Wiki extraction work reached a new kernel milestone, then paused for broader extraction research and a DJClaw article request. The assistant had already switched wiki page generation to the new kernel DB (`nodes/events/relations`), added first-pass publish filters, cleared stale `entries/history/*.html`, and regenerated a cleaner set of 146 node pages while skipping 54 noisy nodes. Before proceeding with extraction-rule improvements (`2.1` tighter entity extraction, `2.2` canonicalization/alias merge), the user asked for external research on existing extraction tools, LLM-assisted skills/plugins, and a more comprehensive future extraction strategy. Brave search was unavailable, so the assistant used direct fetches of official docs/repos and summarized a layered recommendation: Instructor for structured extraction, LlamaIndex property-graph ideas for graph-shaped design, BAML / DSPy for later engineering/eval optimization, and GraphRAG as long-term architecture reference. The user then requested a concise DJClaw article summarizing the original extraction idea, what had actually been implemented so far, and the future options; assistant checked the DJClaw repo, confirmed latest post number 069, inspected `index.html`, `sitemap.xml`, and recent post templates, and began drafting/publishing the new article as post 070.

[2026-03-25 23:13] Wiki extraction PoC moved from design into implementation. User approved using recent 1-week HISTORY samples and current models; assistant created `wiki/docs/EXTRACTION-POC-PLAN.md` and `wiki/scripts/extraction_poc.py`, confirmed recent 7-day sample size (~12–13 entries), verified Gemini HTTP access with `GEMINI_API_KEY`, integrated Gemini 2.5 Flash via direct HTTP (no SDK/pydantic), and produced `wiki/data/extraction-poc/structured-candidates.json`. First Gemini run was too noisy (236 nodes / 247 relations / 60 events across 12 entries), then prompt tightening + local post-processing reduced output to 36 nodes / 24 relations / 16 events across 13 entries with 5 parse errors remaining. User then instructed assistant to do A/B/C in parallel: fix parse errors, add normalization, write a baseline comparison note, and also test Groq with the most advanced available model if possible.

[2026-03-25 23:22] Wiki extraction PoC work continued. User asked to do A/B/C together: fix remaining parse errors, add normalization, and write a baseline comparison note, while preferring Gemini or Groq and asking to use the most advanced available model. Assistant edited `wiki/scripts/extraction_poc.py` multiple times, first switching to Gemini Pro priority with 429 retry and stronger normalization, then discovered `gemini-2.5-pro` was unusable on the current free tier (13/13 requests hit HTTP 429 quota errors), so reverted default back to `gemini-2.5-flash`. A new comparison script `wiki/scripts/baseline_recent_history_compare.py` and note `wiki/docs/EXTRACTION-COMPARISON-NOTES.md` were created; baseline recent-window output showed top entities like DJClaw, Git, GitHub, Logseq, trips, wiki, and New Orleans, while Flash PoC only partially succeeded because quota remained the main bottleneck. Assistant concluded the real issue is provider quota rather than parser logic, recommended adding resume/skip-completed plus slow batch execution next, and then investigated the user’s claim that Groq might still be available. Shell env checks showed no `GROQ_API_KEY` in `~/.profile`, `~/.bashrc`, or current env, but the user clarified Groq is in config; assistant verified `~/.nanobot/config.json` and `.bak` contain a `groq` section, confirming Groq credentials/config likely exist in nanobot config rather than shell env. Useful files touched/created: `wiki/scripts/extraction_poc.py`, `wiki/scripts/baseline_recent_history_compare.py`, `wiki/docs/EXTRACTION-COMPARISON-NOTES.md`, `wiki/data/extraction-poc/baseline-recent-history.json`, and refreshed `wiki/data/extraction-poc/structured-candidates.json`.

[2026-03-26 00:03] Wiki extraction PoC provider/model work advanced and the user selected Groq as the main extraction provider. Assistant verified nanobot config contains readable provider keys for Groq/Gemini/OpenAI, rewrote `wiki/scripts/extraction_poc.py` to support env→`~/.nanobot/config.json` fallback plus `--provider/--model/--limit/--days`, and validated Groq/OpenAI while Gemini was blocked by 429 quota. Groq model discovery against the live API showed available text models including `llama-3.3-70b-versatile`, `moonshotai/kimi-k2-instruct`, `openai/gpt-oss-120b`, `qwen/qwen3-32b`, and `meta-llama/llama-4-scout-17b-16e-instruct`; a 5-entry A/B on `llama-3.3-70b-versatile`, `moonshotai/kimi-k2-instruct`, and `openai/gpt-oss-120b` found all three parse-stable, with `llama-3.3-70b-versatile` the most balanced current default for nodes+relations+events, Kimi the backup challenger, and `gpt-oss-120b` weak on relations. User approved continuing with Groq as the default main model and also requested a deeper explanation of the wiki pipeline layers (the 5–6 layer design from extraction through materialization), how the current PoC maps onto those layers, examples, and a cartoon-poster visualization using an OpenAI image model, to be published on DJClaw. Assistant started subagent `wiki-layers-poster-note` for that architecture/poster/article package, confirmed DJClaw repo path `/home/dj/.nanobot/workspace/djclaw.github.io`, corrected an initial post-numbering detection mistake by listing repo files directly, and determined the next DJClaw post number should be 071. Assistant also verified OpenAI/Groq/Gemini keys are readable from config and began checking DJClaw post templates plus possible OpenAI Images API availability for generating the poster asset.

User also requested a deeper scheduler design for daily ingestion of new HISTORY content through extraction/build/db/page generation and automatic GitHub push; subagent `nanobot-daily-wiki-scheduler` was started (id 336e7dc7) to investigate whether nanobot scheduling should live in heartbeat/cron/another layer.

[2026-03-26 07:20] User reported wiki extraction logic still felt too loose after reviewing several extracted entities, and asked to use a stricter logic plus the Kimi model so final entities look more like stable concrete items such as New York or New Jersey. Assistant inspected `wiki/scripts/extraction_poc.py`, sampled current outputs, ran Groq Kimi (`moonshotai/kimi-k2-instruct`) on recent-history windows, and concluded the current pipeline was still too summary-like, leaving abstract/internal nodes such as workflow names, device/platform terms, and model/provider artifacts. Assistant edited `extraction_poc.py` multiple times to make prompts and local filtering more conservative, reran Kimi on a wider 7-day sample, and proposed the next stricter taxonomy gate: prioritize only place / project / tool-product-service / org-platform / person, while largely dropping topic/other, abstract workflow phrases, temporary task names, device/OS/channel nouns, and model-experiment noise. Earlier in the same conversation, the cropped poster image for DJClaw post 071 was first fixed and pushed in commit `a03cd93`, but after the user reported section 1 still was not fully visible, assistant verified the source image itself was too far left, rebuilt the poster with a full six-column relayout, and pushed the redesigned asset in commit `5ebf885` (`Redesign poster image for post 071`).

[2026-03-26 07:40] Wiki extraction PoC was deemed good enough by the user to merge into the formal extraction pipeline. Before this request, the assistant had already switched the daily recent-history path away from the old rule-based `extract_history.py` to a Kimi-backed flow by making `extract_history.py` a thin wrapper over `scripts/extraction_poc.py`, updating `extract_history_recent.py`, and adding default Groq/Kimi env wiring in `run_recent_daily_refresh.sh`. User’s latest instruction: fully merge the PoC into the official extraction pipeline, clean up old code, and audit the wiki extraction/build chain so every step uses the most updated logic.

User then approved cleanup/archive plus pushing this strict v3 round; assistant checked the wiki repo state on branch `main` with remote `https://github.com/djclaw/wiki.git` and prepared to commit/push only the strict-v3-related changes.
